gaps.explanation: Gap 9,922,864 (statement 36,926,493 p7, schedule 27,003,629). (1) Missing fund column: the governmental funds statement (pp6-7, printed pp20-21) prints an 'Other Governmental Funds' column (Total revenues 6,430,156, p7) with no schedule; none of its cells are in detail. Added: Property taxes 531,711, Fees, taxes, permits and licenses 156,970, Sales tax 427,772, Charges for services 989,037, Donations 2,061,392, Grants 228,639, Investment earnings 422,381, Miscellaneous 1,612,254 = 6,430,156. (2) Different basis (printed, not added): the five major funds are in detail from their budget-basis schedules (pp14-18, printed pp54-58), whose printed Total revenues differ from the GAAP columns (pp6-7): General 12,694,121 vs 12,740,246 (-46,125), Streets/Engineering 4,862,691 vs 4,852,256 (+10,435), Sales Tax 6,417,041 vs 6,448,008 (-30,967), 1/2 Cent Sales Tax 2,929,411 vs 2,935,828 (-6,417), ARP Act 100,365 vs 3,519,999 (-3,419,634: the GAAP ARP column prints Grants 3,419,634; the ARP budget schedule p18 prints only Investment income 100,365, no grant receipt). These are the same rows on two bases for funds that already have schedule lines, so no GAAP cell is added on top of the budget-basis lines. Arithmetic: 27,003,629 + 6,430,156 = 33,433,785; 36,926,493 - 33,433,785 = 3,492,708 = 46,125 - 10,435 + 30,967 + 6,417 + 3,419,634 (budget vs GAAP, stays).

gaps.explanation: Gap 2,159,268 (statement 52,007,717 p7, schedule 49,848,449). (1) Missing fund column: Other Governmental Funds column (p7) Total expenditures 4,931,822 = Public safety 2,276,653 + Public works 287,711 + Cultural and recreation 3,907 + Community development 684,289 + Capital outlay 435,242 + Principal 845,000 + Interest and fiscal charges 399,020; added. (2) Different basis (printed, not added): General budget schedule (p14) Total expenditures 36,406,789 (Capital outlay 18,210,618) vs GAAP General column (p6) 33,698,398 (Capital outlay 16,018,674; also Principal on leases 104,281 and Interest on leases 24,250, rows the budget schedule does not print and whose cash is within the budget-basis function/capital lines, so they are not added on top) = +2,708,391; Streets/Engineering budget 12,217,437 (p15) vs GAAP 12,153,274 = +64,163; 1/2 Cent Sales Tax 1,224,223 on both (its budget 'Other' 594,223 = GAAP 'Interest and fiscal charges' 594,223, already detail). Arithmetic: 49,848,449 + 4,931,822 = 54,780,271 = 52,007,717 + 2,772,554 (2,708,391 + 64,163; budget vs GAAP, stays).

gaps.explanation: Gap 1,284,291 (statement 30,082,825 p7; schedule 28,798,534 = General 'Transfers in (out), net' 23,738,538 p14 + Streets/Engineering 5,059,996 p15). (1) Missing fund column: Other Governmental Funds 'Transfers in' 804,291 (p7), added. (2) The GAAP General Fund column (p6) prints Transfers in 24,218,538 and Transfers out (480,000); the General Fund budget schedule (p14) prints only the net 'Transfers in (out), net' 23,738,538, which is already in detail and holds both. Adding the gross 24,218,538 would count that money twice, so it is not added. Arithmetic: 28,798,534 + 804,291 = 29,602,825 = 30,082,825 - 480,000 (net presentation of the printed schedule, stays). SBITA (General 51,459 p6, Other Governmental Funds 472,787 p7) is already in detail (pass 2); no other other-financing row is printed in any governmental column.

gaps.explanation: Gap 10,493,496 (statement 27,943,189 p7; schedule 17,449,693 = Sales Tax (9,265,809) p16 + 1/2 Cent Sales Tax (4,764,250) p17 + ARP Act (3,419,634) p18, each equal to its GAAP column's Transfers out). (1) Missing fund column: Other Governmental Funds 'Transfers out' (10,013,496) (p7), added. (2) The GAAP General Fund column (p6) Transfers out (480,000) is netted inside the General Fund budget line 'Transfers in (out), net' 23,738,538 (p14) already in detail; not added (it would double count). Arithmetic: 17,449,693 + 10,013,496 = 27,463,189 = 27,943,189 - 480,000 (stays).
